name: invader-march
description: The cheapest possible march cycle: one 16x12 crab invader, a copied frame with a single leg-swap edit, and a pingpong tag exported to GIF. The whole animation is two frames that differ only in the legs — the classic space-invader trick — so it costs almost nothing to author yet reads as motion.

steps.note: A 16x12 canvas is the tightest grid that still fits a two-eyed crab with antennae and a 3px leg span on each side. Fresh store, so the id slugifies to 'invader'.

Paint pose-A in one call. Every coordinate is placed as a mirror pair across the col 7|8 centre line (2<->13, 4<->11, ...), so the sprite is symmetric by construction rather than by an axis op that would round on an even width. Body is one green; the two eyes are the only second colour. Antenna stubs (2,3)/(13,3) hang off the head; legs+feet live in rows 8-10.

Catch floating pixels BEFORE animating: a stray would get copied into frame 1 and ruin both. Expect exactly one component covering every opaque pixel — the legs attach to the body diagonally, which 8-connectivity (the default) treats as joined.
Frame 1 starts as a pixel-perfect clone of frame 0, so the body, head, eyes and antennae are guaranteed identical for free — we only have to repaint what moves.

Pose B, the leg swap. The four leg stubs in row 8 stay put; only the lower joints move. Clear rows 9-10 (alpha 0 erases) to wipe pose-A's outward splay, then redraw the legs tucked inward to the opposite phase. The shared body in rows 0-8 is never touched, keeping the edit minimal and the diff clean.

Verify the leg-swap is honest: the diff must be confined to rows 9-10. If any change shows up in the head/eyes/antennae, pose B accidentally disturbed the static body and the march would jitter instead of cycle cleanly.

Tag both frames as 'march'. Pingpong on a 2-frame range plays 0,1,0,1... which is exactly the alternating leg cycle, and it spends no extra frames on turnaround (no inner frames between two endpoints).

A pingpong loop reverses at its ends, so there is no last->first hard cut to worry about; the audit returns seam_score 0 by construction. Running it documents that the loop is seamless rather than leaving the reader to assume it.
Render the 'march' tag at 6x (96x72) so the pixels are legible. A plain filename keeps the GIF in the caller's cwd; the recipe stays agnostic about where that is.
